subject: ready-for-life

location.courseTitle: Ready for Life 11: Postsecondary Planning and Portfolio

instructions: Complete the task or its stated simulation alternative. Do not submit photos, recordings, addresses, account details, or private household information.
Learner completion never certifies a guardian-authority task; those tasks remain pending until a guardian attests.

learnerTasks.directions: Before building the plan, gather what you already have from this unit.
learnerTasks.prompt: Looking back at this unit, which piece (record-keeping categories, describing a concern, or recognizing urgency) do you feel most confident about already, and which do you still want this plan to help with?

learnerTasks.directions: Build the three parts of your personal health-management plan.
learnerTasks.prompt: Build a contact list template organized by type of need (for example: routine/preventive care, urgent concerns, questions between visits). For each type, name the role of who to contact and where the actual contact information is kept -- not the real contact information itself.

learnerTasks.directions: Build the three parts of your personal health-management plan.
learnerTasks.prompt: Write a short description of how your personal records will be kept: what categories, where stored, and who can see them, building on the template from earlier in this unit.

learnerTasks.directions: Build the three parts of your personal health-management plan.
learnerTasks.prompt: Write your own short version of the urgency rule from earlier in this unit: what signs mean 'seek help now' versus 'can wait,' in your own words.

learnerTasks.directions: Review the finished plan with a guardian.
learnerTasks.prompt: I reviewed all three parts of the plan with a guardian.

learnerTasks.directions: Review the finished plan with a guardian.
learnerTasks.prompt: My guardian confirmed the plan is realistic for our household (for example, the contact types make sense and the record-keeping location is one we'd actually use).

learnerTasks.directions: Reflect on the plan as a whole.
learnerTasks.prompt: Now that the plan exists, what is the one part you're most likely to actually use in the next few months, and why?

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated Plan completeness across the three parts criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated Appropriate level of detail (role and location, not real private detail) criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated Guardian review substance criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the assessed objective.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Health and Wellness Self-Management?
